deep.reconstruction:
The page has three parts: reduction terms for Arcturus, a level-bubble/temperature table, and test readings of a new spirit level.

A. Apparent declination of Arcturus, 1818 (continues the previous page). The column headers 298°25', 320°9', 326° are phase constants. The three logarithms are amplitudes:
- 1.0949 gives 12.44";
- 0.9002 gives 7.95";
- 9.664 (i.e. -10) gives 0.461".

The rows are dated Aug 10, Aug 20, Aug 30 and Sept 9. For each date three arguments are tabulated, written as degrees.minutes:
- Sun's longitude ☉: 137°21', 146°57', 156°34', 166°13'. These continue the previous page's 99°14' (Jul 1) at about 9°33' per 10 days.
- Lunar node ☊: 33°23', 32°51', 32°20' (exactly 32°19'), 31°48'. It regresses about 32' per 10 days.
- 2☉: 274°42', 293°54', 313°08' (written 313.8), 332°26'.

Below these Gauss lists log sin(☉+298°25'), log sin(☊+320°9') and log sin(2☉+326°), with n marking negative sines. I verified every entry:
- ☉+298°25' = 75°46', 85°22', 94°59', 104°38'; the logs are 9.9865, 9.9986, 9.9984, 9.9857.
- ☊+320°9' = 353°32', 353°0', 352°29', 351°57'; the logs are 9.0516n, 9.0859n, 9.1167n, 9.1462n.
- 2☉+326° = 240°42', 259°54', 279°08', 298°26'; the logs are 9.941n, 9.993n, 9.994n, 9.944n.

The products feed the table on the previous page. That table gives Δδ = (precession + proper motion) + 12.44 sin(☉+298°25') + 7.95 sin(☊+320°9') + 0.461 sin(2☉+326°). In modern terms these are the annual aberration, the lunar nutation term (18.6 yr) and the semi-annual solar nutation term.

Check for Aug 10: 12.44·0.9693 = +12.06, 7.95·(−0.1126) = −0.89, 0.461·(−0.872) = −0.40. With −11.57 the total is −0.80, as on the previous page.

The secular column falls 0.52" per 10 days, about −19"/yr. This matches precession 20.0"·cos 212° ≈ −17" plus Arcturus' proper motion of about −2". These are star constants of Bessel day-number type for reducing meridian-circle declinations.

B. Right-hand column of 18 pairs: temperature (presumably Réaumur) and bubble length of the level. Gauss underlines the mean 8.4 | 108.6. Exactly: Σt = 151.2/18 = 8.40 and ΣL = 1954.1/18 = 108.56.

The last three pairs repeat the Oct 26–27 entries of the main table: (8.1, 113.8), (9.0, 110.5), (9.0, 108.9).

C. 'Neue Libelle' (new level), Oct 26 – Nov 10 (1817). Each row has three readings:
- an angle near 1'17"–1'20" (its meaning cannot be fixed from this page; daily means appear on the next page);
- the bubble length;
- the temperature.

Bubble length visibly rises as temperature falls, as expected from liquid contraction.

'm. Hel aus (48)' is a grand mean over 48 observations. These are the 23 + 10 tabulated rows plus the first 15 pairs of the right column (my reconstruction). Then Σt = 386.1 and 386.1/48 = 8.044, matching 8.04. Also ΣL = 5352.8 and 5352.8/48 = 111.52, matching 111.52 (this needs the Nov 6 overwritten value 111.5).

Gauss then splits the observations into three equal temperature classes, presumably 16 each:
- 6.75° gives 116.01;
- 8.09° gives 112.86;
- 9.29° gives 105.68.

The class means average back to 8.043 and 111.52. This implies a slope of about −4.1 length units per degree; the slope is my inference and is not written on the page.

The final note '1" = 5⅓ mm' gives the scale value of the new level: 1 arcsecond of tilt equals 5⅓ mm of bubble travel. The next page refines this to 5.31 mm (new) against 3.07 (old), ratio about 9:5.
errors: Node argument for Aug 30 written 32°20' where the steady −32'/10 days progression gives 32°19'; the effect on the log sine is negligible.
Nov 6 third row: bubble length and temperature are overwritten. The grand mean 111.52 requires 111.5 (not 110.5).

results.what: Tabulated apparent-place declination corrections for Arcturus: aberration 12.44" sin(☉+298°25'), lunar nutation 7.95" sin(☊+320°9'), solar nutation 0.461" sin(2☉+326°), plus precession/proper motion
results.modern_name: Star constants / Besselian day numbers for apparent place reduction
results.usually_credited_to: Standard practice c. 1800–1830 (Delambre, Zach; systematized by Bessel, Tabulae Regiomontanae 1830)

results.what: Mean bubble length versus temperature of a new spirit level, with grand mean from 48 observations and three temperature classes
results.modern_name: Temperature calibration of a spirit level (bubble-length variation)

results.what: Scale value of the new level: 1" = 5⅓ mm of bubble run
results.modern_name: Level sensitivity (angular value of a division)

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine observatory reductions of 1817–18: apparent-place terms for Arcturus and calibration of a new level against temperature. Gauss's work on Göttingen meridian observations and instruments is well known.

checkable.asserts: Equals about 9.0516 (Aug 10 node term, negative sine).
Equals about −0.80, the Aug 10 total on the previous page.
Grand means over 48 observations are 8.044 and 111.517.
The three equal temperature classes average back to 8.043 and 111.517.

transcription_corrections: Nov 6 third row: read bubble length 111.5 and temperature 7.4 (overwrites); confirmed by the 48-observation mean 111.52.
'm. Hel aus (48)' is plausibly 'Mittel aus (48)' (mean of 48 observations). The arithmetic confirms a 48-observation mean, and '8"04' is a mean temperature 8.04, not arcseconds.
Right column third entry reads 110.8 (overwritten); consistent with the column mean 108.56.
In the left table the bracket '} 9.0' applies to both Oct 27 rows (110.5 and 108.9).
